text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The United States is not going to undertake a separate initiative on the Cyprus dispute at present beyond that underway by the United Nations.
- Visits across the Green Line dividing Cyprus create good will between the two communities and help efforts to find a political settlement of the Cyprus dispute, says the government.

- Populist and contradictory policies of the government are revealed. It has terminated the policy of "joint decisions" with the Greek government on issues relating to the Cyprus issue although it will not officially come out and say so.
- Nicosia agrees with attempts by the Greek government to improve its relations with Turkey.
- Occupancy levels in hotels are 30 to 40 percent lower this April compared to April 1996, say hoteliers.

- Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash wants everything. He agrees on including United Nations ideas and paragraphs of UN resolutions in talks, but reserves the right to give his own interpretation of political equality and sovereignty.
- Centre-right Diko party leader Kyprianou will table a request at the National Council meeting tomorrow for a conference on the Cyprus problem involving Greek and Greek Cypriot parties.
